Group B *streptococcus* (GBS), also known as *Streptococcus agalactiae*, is recognized as a leading cause of postpartum infection and neonatal sepsis. Infection in healthy, nonpregnant adults is becoming more common, especially among young to middle-aged women with diabetes. Signs and symptoms of GBS infection include the following:. It is primarily seen in older adults with diabetes or with a variety of neurologic deficits; its presentation is the same as that of any bacterial pneumonia (fever, shortness of breath, chest pain, pleuritic pain, cough). In adults, GBS meningitis is associated with a variety of anatomic abnormalities that are complications of neurosurgery. ·    Skin and soft-tissue infection, decubitus ulcers, and colonization of foot infections in patients with diabetes also can result from GBS infection. results.title: Performances of two rapid LAMP-based techniques for the intrapartum detection of Group B Streptococcus vaginal colonization | Annals of Clinical Microbiology and Antimicrobials | Springer Nature Link
results.content: # Performances of two rapid LAMP-based techniques for the *intrapartum* detection of Group B *Streptococcus* vaginal colonization. Group B *Streptococcus* (GBS) is the leading cause of invasive infections in newborns. The prevention of GBS neonatal disease relies on the administration of an *intrapartum* antibiotic prophylaxis to GBS-colonized women. In recent years, rapid *intrapartum* detection of GBS vaginal colonization using real-time nucleic acid amplification tests (NAATs) emerged as an alternative to antenatal culture screening methods. We compared the performances of two loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP) tests, the Ampliflash® GBS and the PlusLife® GBS tests, to standard culture for GBS detection in vaginal specimens from pregnant women. The Ampliflash® GBS test and the PlusLife® GBS tests gave a result for 100% and 96.3% tests, respectively. False negative results of the Ampliflash® GBS test correlated with low-density GBS cultures. Time-to-results correlated with GBS culture density only for the PlusLife® GBS test (*p* < 0.001).
